notes: The 6507 in the 2600 is a 6502 with 13 address lines (8 KB space, cartridge at $1000-$1FFF) and no IRQ/NMI pins.
CPU clock is the colour clock / 3: 76 CPU cycles per scanline (228 colour clocks).
Indexed reads (abs,X / abs,Y / (zp),Y) take +1 cycle when the effective address crosses a page; stores and read-modify-write instructions already include that cycle in their fixed count.
Branches: 2 cycles not taken, 3 taken, 4 taken to another page.
Zero-page indexed addressing wraps inside page 0 ($FF,X with X=2 reads $01).

Size and cycles of all 256 opcodes agree between masswerk.at, groepaz's 'No More Secrets' and the opcode table in Gopher2600; the 'dasm' flag records whether DASM 2.20.14.1 can emit the opcode from a mnemonic (false = use .byte).

Unstable illegal opcodes (groepaz): SHA, SHX, SHY, SHS/TAS (unreliable address-high-byte group) and ANE, LXA (magic constant). JAM is deterministic but marked unstable here because it freezes the CPU.

acc.name: Accumulator (DASM takes no operand: write ASL, not ASL A)

ADC.description: A = A + M + C. In decimal mode (SED) the addition is BCD; on the NMOS 6502 the N, V and Z flags are not reliable after a decimal ADC (Bruce Clark's decimal-mode tutorial describes the exact behaviour).

ASL.description: Shifts left one bit; bit 7 goes to C, 0 enters bit 0.

BCC.description: Branches if C = 0. 2 cycles, +1 if taken, +1 more if the target is on another page than the next instruction.

BCS.description: Branches if C = 1. 2 cycles, +1 if taken, +1 more if the target is on another page.

BEQ.description: Branches if Z = 1. 2 cycles, +1 if taken, +1 more if the target is on another page.

BMI.description: Branches if N = 1. 2 cycles, +1 if taken, +1 more if the target is on another page.

BNE.description: Branches if Z = 0. 2 cycles, +1 if taken, +1 more if the target is on another page.

BPL.description: Branches if N = 0. 2 cycles, +1 if taken, +1 more if the target is on another page.

BVC.description: Branches if V = 0. 2 cycles, +1 if taken, +1 more if the target is on another page.

BVS.description: Branches if V = 1. 2 cycles, +1 if taken, +1 more if the target is on another page.

BIT.description: Z = (A & M) == 0; N and V take bits 7 and 6 of M. Common on the 2600 to test collision and input bits (D7/D6) without touching A. BIT abs is also used as a 'skip next 2 bytes' trick.

BRK.description: One opcode byte, but the return address pushed is PC+2, so the byte after BRK is skipped (DASM emits only $00). Pushes P with B set, sets I and jumps through the vector at $FFFE (seen at $1FFE on the 6507, which has 13 address lines). The 6507 has no IRQ or NMI pin, so BRK is the only way to reach that vector.

CLD.description: D = 0. Power-on state of D is undefined: clear it at start-up.

CLI.description: I = 0. Irrelevant on the 6507 (no IRQ pin).

CMP.description: Computes A - M: C = A >= M, Z = A == M, N = bit 7 of the result.

CPX.description: Computes X - M and sets flags like CMP.

CPY.description: Computes Y - M and sets flags like CMP.

JMP.description: PC = address. Indirect JMP bug: JMP ($xxFF) reads the high byte from $xx00, not from the next page.

JSR.description: Pushes the address of its own last byte (PC+2 of the opcode) and jumps; RTS adds 1 when it returns. With only 128 bytes of RAM shared with variables, every nested JSR costs 2 bytes of stack.

LSR.description: Shifts right one bit; bit 0 goes to C, 0 enters bit 7.

PHP.description: Pushes P with B and bit 5 set. The stack lives in page 1, which on the 2600 mirrors the TIA/RAM area, so if S points at a TIA write register the push writes P into it; because bit 1 of P is Z, one 3-cycle PHP can switch ENAM0, ENAM1 or ENABL (all use bit 1).

RTS.description: Pulls PC and adds 1. Pushing an address-1 and doing RTS is a common jump-table trick.

SBC.description: A = A - M - (1 - C). Set C (SEC) before a single-byte subtraction.

SED.description: D = 1: ADC/SBC work in BCD. Handy for scores.

SEI.description: I = 1. Customary at reset even though the 6507 has no IRQ pin.

STA.description: M = A. STA abs,X / abs,Y and (zp),Y always take the extra cycle.

TXS.description: S = X. Used to aim the stack at a TIA register before a PHP/PHA that writes it (see PHP).

LAX.description: A = X = M. Stable except the immediate form (LXA).

DCP.description: M = M - 1, then compares A with the result as CMP does (C = A >= M, Z = A == M). Saves a separate DEC and CMP; groepaz's document shows loop-counter uses. Documented as DCM/DCP.

ISB.description: M = M + 1, then SBC M. Also known as ISC or INS; DASM spells it ISB.

SLO.description: M = M << 1, then A = A | M.

RLA.description: M = ROL M, then A = A & M.

SRE.description: M = M >> 1, then A = A ^ M.

RRA.description: M = ROR M, then A = A + M + C.

ANC.description: A = A & #imm; C is set to bit 7 of the result (the N flag). Both $0B and $2B do this.

ASR.description: A = (A & #imm) >> 1. Also known as ALR (groepaz's name); DASM spells it ASR.

ARR.description: A = ROR(A & #imm), but C and V are derived from bits 6 and 5 of the result instead of the normal ROR rule (see groepaz's document); decimal mode adds further quirks.

SBX.description: X = (A & X) - #imm; the subtraction ignores the incoming carry, and C, Z, N come out like CMP. Also known as AXS or SAX in older lists; DASM spells it SBX.

USBC.description: Opcode $EB behaves like SBC #imm. DASM has no USBC mnemonic and always assembles SBC #imm as $E9, so $EB needs .byte.

LAS.summary: A = X = S = M AND S (illegal)
LAS.description: A, X and S all receive M & S. Classed as stable by groepaz and masswerk. Also called LAR. Rarely useful.

ANE.description: Result depends on a chip- and temperature-dependent constant: do not use. Also called XAA.

LXA.description: Opcode $AB. A = X = (A | magic) & imm; the constant depends on chip and temperature, so avoid it. Also called LAX #imm, ATX or OAL.

SHA.description: H is the high byte of the target address. Unreliable when indexing crosses a page. Also called AHX or AXA. Avoid.

SHS.description: Also called TAS. Unreliable when indexing crosses a page. Avoid.

SHX.description: Also called SXA or XAS. Unreliable when indexing crosses a page. Avoid.

SHY.description: Also called SYA or SAY. Unreliable when indexing crosses a page. Avoid.

JAM.description: Locks up the processor until reset; 12 opcodes ($02 $12 $22 $32 $42 $52 $62 $72 $92 $B2 $D2 $F2). Also called KIL or HLT. Deterministic, but marked unstable here so the 'stable only' policy rejects it. DASM has no mnemonic: use .byte. The cycle count is 0 because it never finishes.
